basis: Isolated congenital absence of the cerebellar vermis; confined to the central nervous system.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with severe developmental impairment and movement abnormalities; strabismus affects ocular alignment in 1/2 assessed patients.
Defined by progressive sensory pathway degeneration and retinal dystrophy; skeletal and gastrointestinal complications are occasional.
Inherited glomerular disease causing steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome and progressive kidney failure; no immune mechanism established.
Neonatal conjunctival inflammation, predominantly infectious and classified under gonococcal conjunctivitis; definition also includes chemical cases.
Isolated spermatogenic failure affects reproductive germ cells; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ involvement established.
Mitochondrial metabolic encephalopathy; pigmentary retinopathy occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac, hepatic, renal and hearing abnormalities are occasional.
Partial LH resistance impairs Leydig-cell testosterone production, defining a disorder of gonadal endocrine function.
Defective respiratory ciliary clearance causes chronic airway disease; recurrent middle-ear inflammation occurs in 3/6 patients.
Defined by infection directly involving the kidney; other organ damage varies across the constituent infections.
Craniofacial dysostosis, alopecia and malformed ears with hearing loss define syndrome; cleft palate occurs in 3/4. Eyelid coloboma occurs in 1/4.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; structural muscle loss and foot deformity are common: fatty muscle replacement and pes cavus each reported in 2/2.
Chronic fungal infection directly involving skin and subcutaneous tissue.
Neoplasm arising from vascular tissue; additional organ sites vary across this broad tumour group.
Plasmalogen synthesis disorders predominantly cause neurodevelopmental impairment, skeletal dysplasia and cataracts; each common (>30%) across the predominant rhizomelic forms.
CSNK2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability, developmental delay and seizures; facial features do not establish additional organ damage.
Pattern dystrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium affecting the macula; confined to the eye.
Clonal eosinophilic blood and marrow neoplasm; cardiac, pulmonary and skin infiltration vary, with no additional organ reliably established above 30% here.
Primary malignant bone tumour; pulmonary metastatic occupation occurs in roughly 30% or more over the disease course, although estimates vary.
Sclerosing skeletal dysplasia; hearing impairment occurs in 10/67 and anemia is occasional. Proptosis alone does not establish ocular functional damage.
Inherited hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with myocardial disarray, outflow obstruction and heart failure; pulmonary arterial hypertension is cardiovascular.
Benign teratoma arising from the pericardium.
Inflammation confined to the vulva, a reproductive organ; generic inflammation does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism.
Defined by distal phalangeal hypoplasia or absence together with nail hypoplasia or absence; absent fingernails occur in 80-99%.
Disordered neural circadian timing causes sleep-wake dysfunction. Blindness predisposes to the syndrome; altered melatonin rhythm does not establish endocrine gland damage.
